notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2140.tlg001.1st1K-gr: Abbreviations read as: γ° ounce, δρ. drachma, γρ. gramma (scruple). σιδήρου σκόληος, ‘iron scolex’, is obscure. γλοιός, ‘oily sludge’, is the greasy residue of oil. ‘You will find iron’ is as the text has it.

nodes.text: THE *KATABAPHĒ* [DYEING] OF IAMBLICHUS. – Cappadocian salt, 2 drachmas; Italian cinnabar, half an ounce; *arsenikon* [orpiment], 1 ounce; roasted chalcitis, 6 dr.; iron scolex, that is, flakes of ochre, 6 grammata. Some put in iron-copper, 12 dr.; spodium, half an ounce; verdigris, 3 ounces; chrysocolla, 6 dr.; Thracian cadmia, half an ounce. Having ground [them] separately, you will also mix them together; add mandrake juice until it reaches the thickness of oily sludge, and grind until it dries; and add the blood of a sea hare until it again reaches the thickness of oily sludge; and place it (f. 266 v.) in a living reed, at the fourth joint, and having stopped it with a woollen rag, leave it for 14 days; and when you take it you will find iron. Grind this with fragrant wine until it reaches the thickness of oily sludge, and keep it in a shell. Then melt an equal amount of pure gold and throw on the contents of the shell; and melt until it can no longer give off smoke but makes a smell of sulphur; and take it out and let it cool.
